text:
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T13:02:00Z - rolling out canary v3.9.1 to runtime-canary-A (sha abc123). Diff: heartbeat-prefetch enabled. link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/rollouts/8342 :arrow_forward:

sara-sre: watching canary metrics — saw a tail latency jump at 13:04 UTC, sustained for ~2m. CPU on canary hosts spiked and then kernel fallback started. Paging warnings in host logs. :rotating_light:

mike-runtime: copying logs from one canary pod: 
```
[13:04:23] WARN kernel: fallback_to_cpu_path=true, fragmented_kv_cache=high
[13:04:24] WARN runtime: prefetch worker stuck, queue depth 128 -> eviction thrash
[13:04:25] ERROR allocator: page_faults rising, falling back to generic kernels
```

sara-sre: confirmed - multi-host pattern. Throughput dropped ~30%, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s on canary. This looks like paging + kernel fallback, likely tied to the heartbeat-prefetch change in this deploy.

incident-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-2926801234 - High latency/throughput regression on runtime canary. Paging detected. Paging advisory sent to #eng-oncall. Paging level: SEV-2. Paging people: @sara-sre, @mike-runtime, @lee-eng

lee-eng: I'm on it. Sara — can you confirm whether this is affecting any Dedicated or Prod routes or only canary slice?

john-cs: saw one support ticket from an enterprise customer (acme-corp) around 13:06 complaining about timeouts. They were on prod route but routed through a canary model variant for rollout testing. Looks customer-facing.

anna-pm: please triage customer impact asap. If rollback or kill-switch needed we need a short note for CS to send.

mike-runtime: hypothesis: heartbeat-prefetch is creating additional background KV prefetch threads that increase memory pressure for long sequences, pushing some hosts into kernel fallback path. Kernel fallback disables optimized attention kernels -> big tail increase + batch coalescing misbehavior. Quick mitigation options: 1) toggle feature flag to disable heartbeat-prefetch (fast) 2) rollback rollout (slower, impacts all canary hosts) 3) reduce canary traffic slice (cheap). I recommend flip kill-switch first.

lee-eng: agreed - flip flag on canary slices only. Mike, paste the command you want ops to run.

mike-runtime: run this to flip the flag for the canary tag: 
```
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"\
  "https://ops.redwood.internal/flags/heartbeat_prefetch/toggle"\
  -d '{"target":"runtime-canary-A","enabled":false}'
```

sara-sre: I'll run it now from bastion and watch metrics.

sara-sre: (running) `curl ...` -> 200 OK, flag disabled for runtime-canary-A. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Flag toggle recorded: heartbeat_prefetch=OFF for runtime-canary-A by sara-sre (13:08:14 UTC).

mike-runtime: monitoring - enable additional tracing on canary to verify kernel paths.

sara-sre: within 60s we see p95 drop to ~160ms, throughput back to baseline, page_fault rate begins to normalize. No further kernel fallback logs in last 90s. Looks like kill-switch worked. :thumbsup:

john-cs: CS update: sent note to acme-corp acknowledging transient timeouts, fixed by configuration rollback; told them root cause being experimental prefetch flag. Customer acknowledged and appreciated the quick response.

anna-pm: good. Keep me posted if this needs a full rollback or if scoped flag off is fine for next release. Also we need comms for customers in the impacted cohort.

lee-eng: quick postmortem notes that we'll capture: 1) heartbeat-prefetch creates persistent threads that increase memory footprint in certain sequences 2) autoscale/eviction heuristics interacted poorly causing eviction loops -> kernel fallback 3) canary slice routing allowed customer exposure. Actions: revert the feature from the release branch, add an automatic safety that disables prefetch when mem pressure or page_faults > threshold, add e2e / perf test for long-sequence memory usage before rollout, and add rollout policy to avoid routing enterprise customers to canary variants during risky runtime changes.

mike-runtime: logging + metric hooks to detect early kernel-fallback signatures will be added to the runtime. I'll open RFC and a hotfix patch.

sara-sre: creating incident follow-up doc and linking graphs. Also will schedule oncall handoff notes for the rest of day.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation applied (flag off). Incident severity downgraded to SEV-3. Incident owner: lee-eng. Postmortem assignee: mike-runtime.

lee-eng: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate rollback of the change from the release branch and ensure we flip the flag off in any other canary pools. If we don't see recurrence in 24h we can close.

sara-sre: closing monitoring loop for runtime-canary-A, leaving incident open for postmortem.

mike-runtime: attaching a short repro snippet for the postmortem: 
```
# reproduce load
python tools/loadgen.py --model gpt-large --seq 8192 --qps 50 --enable-heartbeat-prefetch
```

lee-eng: logged action items in the incident tracker: https://infra.redwood/incident/INC-2926801234/actions

anna-pm: thanks team. CS and Sales notified. We'll draft a customer note if required.

sara-sre: oncall handoff to nightshifts in 40m — leaving notes in #eng-oncall.
